branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Opposition softens enough for modified rollout rather than hard postponement.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Parent coalition messaging shifts from stop/pause language to conditional acceptance; union remains non-escalatory; board majority avoids formal pause.
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Parent demands are specific and potentially satisfiable; conflict is not yet maximal.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Superintendent offers independent privacy review, translated notice, and clear family choice mechanism before launch.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Board postpones pilot pending review even if educational case remains attractive.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Board majority publicly references process integrity or asks counsel/procurement for formal justification.
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Process legitimacy can override substantive enthusiasm because authority sits with governance structures.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Questioning board members secure agenda time, document requests, or majority concern over emergency exception.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: District determines contract is too costly to defend and cancels or rebids.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: District messaging shifts from implementation details to alternative vendor/process exploration.
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Vendor owns key terms and remediation pace, creating switching-cost tension.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Vendor refuses plain-language opt-in/out revisions, independent review cooperation, or accelerated multilingual remediation.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Deployment is paused externally or quasi-externally while review proceeds.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: District cites pending external review as reason for delay; regulator correspondence becomes part of public narrative.
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Formal external process can rapidly change risk calculus even if internal actors were leaning toward launch.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Complaint is filed and regulator signals inquiry or caution before launch.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Pilot launches substantially as planned with limited changes.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: District communications emphasize urgency and readiness; opposition remains issue-specific and not mass mobilized.
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Many families are still low-attention, and institutional inertia favors proceeding absent a focal shock.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Concerns remain fragmented, no major board coalition forms, and vendor offers cosmetic assurances.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A launch with meaningful consent/privacy redesign should be classified under guardrailed_launch, not full_launch.
endpoint_ledger.description: District launches the grades 7-9 pilot in six middle schools substantially as originally planned, with only minor non-structural modifications.
endpoint_ledger.label: Full launch

meta.important_question: By week 10, does TutorPilot launch substantially as planned, launch only with added safeguards/narrowing, or fail to launch?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Institutional inertia and urgency support this path if opposition stays fragmented.
realization_criteria: Pilot is operating in all or nearly all planned schools by week 10
No board-imposed postponement remains in effect
No material opt-in/opt-out or independent review requirement was added as a condition of launch
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Launch momentum exists, but multiple unresolved legitimacy issues keep this endpoint contested rather than dominant at T0.

blockers: board preference for full pause instead of conditional launch
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If deployment is delayed beyond week 10 pending review, classify as postponement even if guardrails are being negotiated.
endpoint_ledger.description: District proceeds with rollout only after adding substantive privacy, consent, translation, accessibility, or labor-use safeguards, possibly with narrowed scope.
endpoint_ledger.label: Guardrailed launch

meta.important_question: Does the emergency instructional-services exception withstand board scrutiny, or does procurement legitimacy force postponement or rebid?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Most opposition is conditional rather than absolute, making negotiated modification a strong contender.
realization_criteria: Launch conditions include at least one material safeguard such as opt-in/opt-out clarity, independent privacy review, translated notices, dashboard-use restrictions, or reduced scope pending remediation
Board and district publicly frame launch as modified or conditioned
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: This endpoint aligns with the specific and potentially satisfiable nature of the objections while preserving district urgency.

blockers: Leadership determination to proceed despite controversy
lack of majority board support for intervention
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If contract is rebid, canceled, or externally frozen, use the more specific endpoint rather than postponement.
endpoint_ledger.description: Board or district delays deployment pending procurement, privacy, accessibility, or governance review, without fully canceling the contract by week 10.
endpoint_ledger.label: Postponement pending review

meta.important_question: Are family consent and vendor data-use terms materially changed into a plain-language guardrail regime before deployment?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the cleanest legitimacy-preserving move when time is short and issues are multiple.
realization_criteria: Pilot is not launched by week 10
District or board states review, audit, remediation, or governance process as reason for delay
Contract remains technically alive or unresolved rather than terminated
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Formal procurement doubt plus unresolved equity/privacy issues make delay a credible central outcome.

blockers: High switching costs and urgency around learning support
institutional reluctance to admit process error
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A temporary delay while preserving the contract should remain postponement, not cancellation.
endpoint_ledger.description: District cancels the TutorPilot deal or decides to rebid rather than proceed under current terms.
endpoint_ledger.label: Contract cancellation or rebid

meta.important_question: Does any external complaint or regulator action become the operative cause of deployment pause by week 10?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Termination requires stronger coalition durability and acceptance of operational setback than is yet visible.
realization_criteria: District formally terminates the contract, withdraws the pilot, or initiates a rebid/reprocurement by week 10
Public rationale centers on untenable terms, process defects, or inability to remediate in time
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Plausible if vendor proves inflexible or procurement defect becomes indefensible, but not yet the default at T0.

blockers: Internal actors may resolve dispute before outside action matures
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Internal postponement absent documented external process should not be coded as legal_or_regulatory_hold.
endpoint_ledger.description: An external complaint, legal process, or regulator action becomes the operative force pausing deployment.
endpoint_ledger.label: Legal or regulatory hold

meta.important_question: Does any external complaint or regulator action become the operative cause of deployment pause by week 10?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: External leverage exists as a threat, though evidence of active filing is not yet present.
realization_criteria: By week 10, district cites external complaint, regulator inquiry, or legal directive as cause of pause
Deployment does not proceed because of that external process rather than solely internal choice
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: This endpoint is plausible but contingent on escalation beyond the current record.

initial_events.expected_impact: Raises legitimacy threshold for launch and opens coalition path with board skeptics.

merge_hypotheses.mechanism: All major actors acknowledge tutoring need, making compromise around safeguards more plausible than absolute rejection.
If district clarifies dashboard limits and improves notices, teacher and parent coalitions may partially demobilize even without perfect trust.
A board-directed review or temporary delay could restore enough procedural confidence for a later narrowed rollout.
Fast multilingual fixes and revised family choice terms could reconcile equity and privacy objections without abandoning contract.
